evidence.quote: Use this for calling operations that require authorization from a selling partner.
The LWA access token expires one hour after it is issued.
You must have a professional selling account to develop SP-API private seller applications. Individual accounts are not eligible.
You must be a primary account user to complete registration.
You can self-authorize your application in draft status because there is no reason to publish a private application.
As of April 2022, public and private applications are subject to authorization limits and restrictions.
Explore practical examples and sample implementations in the Selling Partner API Samples repository.

result.notes: SP-API uses Login with Amazon (LWA) OAuth2 tokens (bearer, x-amz-access-token header); the older mandatory AWS SigV4 request signing was deprecated in 2023. There is no free/anonymous dev sandbox: private (self-authorized) seller apps require a Professional Selling Plan account ($39.99/mo, individual accounts explicitly ineligible), and private vendor apps require an existing (invite-only) Vendor Central account; public apps additionally require Appstore listing/review. API surface spans dozens of sub-APIs (Orders, Catalog, Listings, Feeds, Reports, FBA Inventory/Inbound/Outbound, Pricing, Vendor Orders/Shipping/Invoices, Notifications, etc.), totaling well over 300 operations. An MCP server (sp-api-dev-mcp) is published from Amazon's own amzn GitHub org / npm scope @amazon-sp-api-release, treated here as official though I could not fetch its README directly to fully confirm maintainer status (moderate confidence on that specific point).
result.one_liner: Amazon Selling Partner API (SP-API) lets developers programmatically manage Amazon seller/vendor operations — orders, inventory, listings, pricing, fulfillment, and reports.
